PINOY DLG • REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE Lega! Opinion No. 55 s. 2011 AUG 17 2011 MAYOR LUSITO E. MARTY Sta. Cruz, Zambales Dear Mayor Marty: This has reference to your request for this Department's legal opinion on the following quoted queries, to wit: 1. 2. 3. What powers does a Municipal Mayor have anent the issuance or revocation of business permits for/of a mining company which violates the environmental laws or the conditions set forth it its permits/licenses, or which fails to submit the documentary requirements vis-a-vis the latter's applications ? May I stop a mining company from exclusively using a public road, which company converted into its "private road" ? In the implementation of closure orders for entities operating without valid business permits, may the Mayor utilize its local police to assist the local BPLO? We answer all your queries in the AFFIRMATIVE. Anent the first query, may it be stated that Local Government Units (LGUs) are expressly vested with the police power under what is known as the General Welfare Clause now embodied in Section 16 as follows: General Welfare, — Every local government Sec. 16 unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. Along that line, section 444 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides: Sec. 444 The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation.

(b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: xxx (3) (iv) Issue licenses and permits and suspend or revoke the same for any violation of the conditions upon which said licenses or permits had been issued, pursuant to law or ordinance (emphasis ours); Perforce, being the head of the LGU concerned, you are bound by law to ensure that business entities operating thereat are fully complying with both the national and local laws. Thus, a nationally-granted permit does not divest the local government unit where the said establishment is operating, of its power to ensure that all laws are complied with and to restrain within the bounds of the law, and subject to the observance of due process, the operations of the said entity, if the circumstances so warrant. As regards your second query, please be advised that public roads are to be used for public purposes and it is your mandated duty to ensure that the public is not denied access to the said public road, neither is it being privately used by any business. As to your final query, RA 7160 emphatically provides that a Municipal Mayor shall: "Act as the deputized representative of the National Police Commission, formulate the peace and order plan of the municipality and upon its approval, implement the same and exercise general and operational control and supervision over the local police forces in the municipality in accordance with R.A. No. 6975;" Given the above basis, deploying your local police to assist your BPLO for the lawful reason you have stated, is valid and legal. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, JESUS D EIV Direc or III LD: 7/11
